newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia-Belarus union should be considered - Kremlin.
newsitem.headline: Russia-Belarus union should be considered - Kremlin.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin has said Russia and Belarus should consider the idea of a referendum in both states over a merger "in one form or another", the Kremlin press secretary said on Monday.
Earlier on Monday a senior Kremlin official suggested that unification between Russia and Belarus could be the best response to NATO's plans to expand eastwards.
Yeltsin's press secretary, Sergei Yastrzhembsky, told a briefing that Yeltsin had expressed the "strategic idea" of a possible merger in a letter to Belarus leader Alexander Lukashenko.
Officially no merger has been proposed between the two neighbouring Slav states which signed an accord last April on forming closer economic and political ties and a loose community.

Yastrzhembsky quoted Yeltsin as saying in his letter to the hardline Lukashenko that the community had become a reality and that serious steps should follow to bring the two former Soviet republics closer together.

A top Kremlin official, speaking last month on condition of anonymity, said the Russian leadership was seriously considering its position over Lukashenko's intention to hold a referendum in March on a possible union.

Interfax news agency quoted Sergei Shakhrai, deputy head of the Kremlin administration, as saying that unification would meet Russia's strategic and economic interests and would add weight to Moscow's international authority.

"Shakhrai considers that the most effective answer to NATO's expansion eastwards would be real unification between Russia and Belarus," Interfax said. "He considers that 1997 gives unique possibilities for a Russian-Belarussian merger," it added.
Lukashenko has made no secret of his desire to be as close to Russia as possible. He said in a Sunday television programme he enjoyed playing the role of "a junior brother" to Yeltsin.
